newsitem.title: UK: UK natgas rangebound again but liquidity recovers.
newsitem.headline: UK natgas rangebound again but liquidity recovers.

text.p: The U.K. spot natural gas market returned to more active trade after an exceptionally thin day on Monday, traders and brokers said, although prices remained stuck in a narrow range.

"It's still trading in the same ranges," said a trader. "There was more bearish sentiment earlier, but it's a very tight range and still a bit directionless. The whole curve has only 0.05 (penny a therm) between the bid and the offer."
But while activity was greater on Tuesday than on Monday, the trader said he expected a quiet week.
"There's a corporate day out on Thursday and then there's a Bank Holiday, so I expect people will do what they have to do and not much more," he added.

Another trader who had done only some time swaps on the OTC market said he had also been active on IPE futures. He said he was gratified by the fact that 300 lots had been traded on the new balance of the month contract, which had got off to a hesitant start before trading for the first time on Monday.

But while the IPE traded a total of 835 lots, its second best day ever, that market was also rangebound. Apart from the balance of the month contract, which weakened by 0.11 penny a therm, there was no price movement of more than 0.06 penny. And a broker on the OTC market said that physical prices were unchanged for the second day running.
